question: Imatinib (a BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor) is first-line treatment for chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) because the Philadelphia chromosome translocation t(9;22) creates a constitutively active BCR-ABL fusion kinase that is specifically targeted by imatinib.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. CML = Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) = BCR-ABL fusion kinase = imatinib target. Imatinib produces complete cytogenetic remission in the majority of CML patients and is the standard first-line therapy. This is the canonical example of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Philadelphia chromosome [t(9;22)] produces the BCR-ABL fusion oncoprotein — a constitutively active tyrosine kinase. Imatinib competitively inhibits the ATP-binding site of BCR-ABL, revolutionising CML management and achieving >90% complete haematological remission. This is the paradigm example of targeted therapy.
